g.text: Retried — the step is re-entered after a backoff

svg.metadata:
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
# Reference figure for genre `flowchart` — EXPERIMENTAL GENRE (spec/genres/flowchart.md). # Read that status first: `flowchart` is OUTSIDE the v0.1 conformance surface # and outside the compatibility promise (`CONSTRUCT-STATUS-TIERS`), so unlike block.fd there is no # normative/experimental split to make here — EVERY line below is outside the # promise *as written in a flowchart document*, including the ones whose own # status is NORMATIVE. What the split would separate is instead marked per line: # each construct's OWN status is noted where it first appears, because that is # what an author needs when carrying the same construct into `block`. # The set demonstrates every FORM of every keyword, not just every keyword. # Coverage: node tools/reference-coverage.js --strict flowchart figdown 0.2 flowchart title "Job dispatch"
# `class` declares a meaning ONCE; elements join it with class=. The meaning # string is REQUIRED and it is what a reading agent gets instead of a hex value. class retry "Retried — the step is re-entered after a backoff" stroke=#b45309 style=dashed class costly "Long-running — minutes, not seconds" fill=#fef3c7 # A class may declare that it claims NO meaning (`CLASS-EMPTY-MEANING`): the empty # string is a WRITTEN value, not an absent one. Such a class groups attributes # and draws NO legend entry — use it when the colour really is only colour. class tint "" fill=#f8fafc
# `external` is the outside world an edge enters from or leaves to. It is never # drawn as a shape (`EXTERNAL-EDGE-ENDPOINTS`). One at a SOURCE and one at a SINK, so both open ends # of the procedure are stated rather than left to the reader to assume. external queue "from the job queue" external audit "to the audit log"
# ---- the role vocabulary (`FLOWCHART-ROLE-KEYWORDS`) ------------------------------- # Why words and not shapes: a reader who has never opened the spec should get # most of a .fd from the syntax alone. `node q "Valid?" shape=diamond` needs # the drawing convention first; `decision q "Valid?"` is simply read. And the # convention does not even hold — of 216 question-labelled nodes measured in # the production corpus, 78% are diamond, 14% ellipse and 8% carry no shape, # so a reader applying it misreads about a fifth of them. # `terminator`, `process` and `decision` are `node` with a ROLE recorded. They # share the node id namespace and are addressable by edge/pin/rank exactly # like a node. The geometry is DERIVED from the role — rounded, box, diamond — # so a correct flowchart writes no shape= at all. terminator accept "Job accepted" process parse "Parse job descriptor" # A binary branch: the condition rides the EDGE's [mid] label (see below), and # the node's own label asks the question. Nothing else states the branch. decision valid "Descriptor valid?" terminator reject "Rejected" # `class=` takes a comma-separated LIST: channels apply left to right, later # wins per channel. These two touch different channels, so the fill comes from # `costly` and the dash from `retry`. process fetch "Fetch inputs" class=costly,retry
# An n-way dispatch: ONE decision with more than two labelled exits. ISO 5807 # §9.2.2.4 defines the symbol as "a single entry but where there may be a # number of alternative exits", so three or more is the same construct, not a # different one — and the exit VALUES ride the edges exactly as yes/no does. decision kind "Job kind?"
# WITHDRAWN from this genre — the three processes below were wrapped in # `group work "Per-kind work" fill=transparent style=dashed gap=0`, with # `in=work` on each member. `group` was WITHDRAWN from `flowchart` # (`SCENE-KEYWORD-MEMBERSHIP`) on ground (a), no evidence of need: across the whole tree the only # `group` ever written in a flowchart document was this one, in this reference # figure — a keyword demonstrated nowhere but in its own demonstration. It is # KEPT in `block` (89 uses across 5 authored figures) and in `topology`, which # is what a per-genre vocabulary is for (`SUBJECT-VOCABULARY-SCOPE`): one genre's evidence is not # another's. What the box was saying here, `rank build,test,deploy` below still # says, and says as CONTENT rather than as a frame. process build "Compile artifacts" class=costly process test "Run test suite" class=costly process deploy "Roll out release" # A role line MAY still write `shape=` — it overrides the DRAWING only, for an # author who needs a particular picture. The role stays the model (§12.7: # presentation is not meaning on its own), so this is a `process` that happens # to be drawn as an ellipse, and an unfamiliar reader still recovers "process" # from the word rather than from the outline. process other "Record unknown kind" shape=ellipse class=tint
# A bare `node` under `flowchart` is ROLE-UNSTATED, and that is a FOURTH state, # not a defaulted `process` (`UNSAFE-DEFAULT-ELIMINATION` §3 — a default that can assert a falsehood is # not allowed). It says ONE thing: THE SOURCE DOES NOT STATE THE ROLE. Here the # procedure says only "wait and retry", and no clause of it classifies the # stage: ISO 5807 §9.2.1 defines Process as a function "resulting in a change # in value, form or location of information", which a backoff is not, and which # ISO symbol a wait belongs to is not settled in this repository (the standard # was readable only to p. 8 of 25). So this line claims no role rather than # claim a wrong one — and a reading agent sees the difference between "the # author said nothing" and "the author said process". # # What a bare `node` is NOT: a place to park a symbol this genre cannot spell. # Nine ISO stage symbols have no word here (Data, Stored data, Predefined # process, Preparation, Manual operation, Manual input, Document, Parallel # mode, Loop limit), and that is a COVERAGE GAP in FigDown, not a fact about # the figure. When the source DOES state one of them, the interim is `node` # PLUS a comment naming the ISO symbol, so the classification survives as text # a reader can quote: # # node cfg "Read config file" # ISO 5807 Data (input/output) — no role # # and the gap gets reported — the project’s working record keeps it. node backoff "Wait (exponential backoff)" shape=circle class=retry
# WITHDRAWN — `plane over "Overlay" z-index=1` stood here, and the terminator # below carried `plane=over`. The line's own comment used to call `plane` "scene # vocabulary, legal here and identical under block/topology" — that sentence is # the model `SUBJECT-VOCABULARY-SCOPE` dissolved, and the keyword did not survive the audit it invited: # `plane`, `z-index=` and `plane=` were WITHDRAWN from the LANGUAGE # (`PAINT-ORDER-CONSTRUCT`), in every genre, with no replacement spelling. In this genre the ground # was (a), no evidence of need — the only `plane` in any flowchart document in # the tree was the one written above to cover the surface. decision ok "All steps green?" terminator done "Released"
flow down # right|down|left|up — `down` is flowchart's default # `rank` states that these elements are PEERS — same position along the flow # axis. It is CONTENT ("these are alternatives"), not layout, so it survives # the `GUI-WRITEBACK-STRUCTURE` strip test the `layout` zone below does not. rank build,test,deploy
flowline queue -> accept flowline accept -> parse flowline parse -> valid # The branch condition rides the edge's [mid] label and NOTHING else — not the # shape, not the colour, not the rendered position (semantic model, `MEANING-RECOVERY-SOURCE`). flowline valid -[no]-> reject flowline valid -[yes]-> fetch flowline fetch -> kind # Three value-labelled exits plus a fallback: the dispatch value is written on # each edge, so a reading agent can answer "what happens for a test job?". flowline kind -[build]-> build flowline kind -[test]-> test flowline kind -[deploy]-> deploy flowline kind -[other]-> other flowline build -> ok flowline test -> ok flowline deploy -> ok flowline other -> ok flowline ok -[yes]-> done # The CYCLE. FigDown has no loop keyword and needs none: a plain back-edge to # an earlier step IS the loop, and its [mid] label is the loop condition. A # `loop`/`while` construct would state nothing these two lines do not. flowline ok -[no]-> backoff class=retry flowline backoff -> fetch class=retry flowline done -> audit flowline reject -> audit
# Everything below is geometry with no meaning, and a reading agent skips it by # default (`CONTENT-LAYOUT-ZONE-SPLIT`/`GENRE-NAMESPACE`). Removing the whole zone leaves the same figure meaning. layout pin queue at=(150,0) # an external is pinnable exactly like a node pin other width=130 # width only pin backoff width=120 height=40 # both
